entities.summary: Firuzabadi, whose proper name was Abu 'l-Ṭāhir Muḥammad ib Yaʿqūb ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm Majd al-Dīn al-Shāfiʿī al-Shīrāzī, was a Persian Sunni Muslim polymath. He excelled in hadith, grammar, philology, history, literature, poetry and Islamic jurisprudence. He was a revered narrator and preserver of Prophetic traditions. Regarded as a major linguist and one of the prominent scholars of the 15th century. He was one of the leading lexicographers in the medieval Islamic world. He was the compiler of Al-Qāmūs al-Muḥīṭ "The Encompassing Ōkeanós", a comprehensive Arabic dictionary which, for nearly five centuries, was one of the most widely used.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Firuzabadi's Al-Qāmūs al-Muḥīṭ was one of the most widely used Arabic dictionaries for nearly five centuries, shaping Islamic scholarship and language. Its impact can be measured by its enduring influence on lexicography and linguistic studies.
